scope: Proposition 5.11 (Angular separation) of the manuscript “Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation” (preprints/Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-dimensional-wave-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 079 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 79299093c07ea305), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 68. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In an equality quadratic family with c > 0, the conditional (θ, r) law for an admissible side avoids arbitrary affine lines with a positive power. At c = 1 this assertion requires the coarse side with the additional left label slack in Definition 5.8; it is not asserted for a general exact side. More precisely, for a line chosen measurably per Z, its δλ-neighborhood has total probability at most δελ in the exponent limits, for some ε > 0, each tested λ > 0, and sufficiently small h. The constants are uniform on bounded lists of positive λ. In a pure linear family, the analogous statement holds for predicting a value of r. In a clipped classical linear branch with p∗(a) = b1(a), two conditionally independent marks satisfy |ri − rj| ≥ δλ with probability tending to one for every fixed λ > 0; no uniform positive avoidance exponent is asserted in this case.
